answer: Resist sybils with cross-chain collateral mirroring: an identity's weight equals the smallest stake it locks across several independent chains, so one chain's stake cannot mirror into influence on another. An orchard of honest agents stakes once on each chain and keeps full weight. An attacker minting ten thousand fakes in a nebula of names must fund ten thousand stakes on every chain, since splitting capital only shrinks the mirrored minimum. Forging influence costs real capital per identity per chain, while an honest agent stakes once and is done.
